legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code Ch. 37, §§ 37.2 & 37.3(a)(1) (Rent Ordinance Coverage & Annual CPI Cap)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Primary Controlling Cap IF Covered (Pre-June 14, 1979 Multi-Unit Rental)
legal_framework.rule_summary: For covered units, caps annual base-rent increases at 60% of Bay Area CPI-U once every 12 months: 1.6% for effective dates March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (was 1.4% for 3/1/25–2/28/26). Applies to base rent only; rounding up to the nearest dollar is prohibited.

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code § 37.15 & Ch. 37A (Housing Inventory & Rent Increase License)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Mandatory Pre-Condition for Covered Units (Phased in 7/1/22 for 10+ units; 3/1/23 for 1–9 units)
legal_framework.rule_summary: Landlord must submit annual Housing Inventory unit data on the Rent Board Portal (March 1 annual deadline) and hold an active Rent Increase License on the effective date before an annual or banked increase is enforceable.

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(2) & Rent Board Topic 503 (Banked Rent Increases)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Governs Skipped Anniversaries (Requires Date-Specific Ledger Audit)
legal_framework.rule_summary: Skipped annual increases bank only if ≥24 full months pass without any increase. Banked percentages are summed additively (never compounded or prorated), do not carry over to a new tenancy, and must be specified in the written notice.

legal_framework.statute: SF Rent Board Rules & Regs §§ 6.13 & 6.14 (Additional Occupants & Subsequent Occupants)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Governs Unit 1 Occupant Change (Continuing Occupant Tenant A1 + Tenant A4)
legal_framework.rule_summary: Charging extra rent solely for an additional/replacement roommate is unlawful even if stated in a lease (§ 6.13). Market reset under § 6.14 applies ONLY after ALL original occupants permanently vacate AND only if a timely written § 6.14 notice was served without waiver.

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code §§ 37.7 & 37.8 (Petitions & Passthroughs Above Annual Cap)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Exclusive Route for Above-Cap Increases on Covered Units
legal_framework.rule_summary: Any increase above annual + banked CPI requires a prior Rent Board Petition (Capital Improvement, Operating & Maintenance, Comparable Rents, § 1.21) or official Rent Board Passthrough Worksheet (GO Bond, Water Bond, Utility). Tenants need not pay petitioned increases until Rent Board approval.

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code § 37.9 (Just-Cause Eviction Protections — 17 Just Causes as amended by Ord. 003-26)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Applies to Covered SF Residential Tenancies
legal_framework.rule_summary: Lease expiration is NOT cause to evict or compel a new lease at higher rent. Termination requires one of 17 enumerated statutory just causes, with mandatory relocation payments on covered no-fault evictions ($8,245/tenant up to $24,733/unit + $5,497 elderly/disabled/child add-on for 2026–27).

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code § 37.10B (Tenant Harassment — Proposition M)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Applies Citywide to Bad-Faith Landlord Conduct
legal_framework.rule_summary: Prohibits bad-faith coercive rent demands, repair neglect, privacy intrusions, retaliation, or housing discrimination; provides civil remedies of treble actual damages (or $1,000 statutory minimum), injunctive relief, criminal misdemeanor penalties, and mandatory prevailing-tenant attorney's fees.

legal_framework.statute: SF Admin. Code § 37.10C (Ordinance Nos. 224-24 & 169-25 — Ban on Algorithmic Rent-Setting)
legal_framework.rule_summary: Bans using revenue-management software analyzing non-public competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels ($1,000 civil penalty per unit per month + prevailing-tenant attorney's fees). Effective Oct. 6, 2025, SF tenants' rights organizations have direct statutory standing to sue.

legal_framework.statute: Cal. Civil Code § 827 & Code Civ. Proc. § 1013 (Written Notice & Fixed-Term Bar)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Mandatory Notice Procedure & Unit 1 Contract Gate
legal_framework.rule_summary: Unilateral rent-increase notices apply ONLY to periodic (week-to-week/month-to-month) tenancies—not during an active fixed-term lease unless expressly permitted by the lease. Requires ≥30 days written notice if ≤10% (12-month cumulative) or ≥90 days if >10%, served personally or by U.S. mail (+5 calendar days inside CA).

legal_framework.statute: Cal. Civil Code § 1954.53 (Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Bars Vacancy Decontrol While Original Occupant Remains
legal_framework.rule_summary: Authorizes market initial rent when a unit is vacant (or exempt single-family/condo where criteria are met), but § 1954.53(d)(2)–(3) expressly bars vacancy increases on partial occupancy changes while at least one original occupant pursuant to the rental agreement remains in lawful possession.

legal_framework.statute: Cal. Civil Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482 — Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Yields to Stricter SF Rent Ordinance Cap (§ 1947.12(d)(7))
legal_framework.rule_summary: Caps non-exempt California units at 5% + CPI (8.8% in SF for 8/1/26–7/31/27), but explicitly exempts units governed by a local ordinance restricting rent increases to a lower amount. Does NOT authorize 8.8% increases on SF Rent Ordinance units.

Subsection (a) bars increasing rent within 180 days of specified tenantability complaints, agency inspections, or citations if the tenant is not in default; subsection (d) separately prohibits increasing rent at any time in retaliation for a tenant peaceably exercising any right under the law or organizing.

legal_framework.statute: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA) & Civil Code § 51 (Unruh Civil Rights Act)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Applies to All California Rental Terms & Notices
legal_framework.rule_summary: Bars housing discrimination, harassment, discriminatory inquiries/notices, and retaliation based on race, color, ancestry, national origin, citizenship/immigration status, primary language, religion, sex/gender, LGBTQ+ status, marital/familial status, source of income (vouchers), disability, age, military/veteran status, or genetic info.

legal_framework.statute: Federal Fair Housing Act, 42 U.S.C. §§ 3604(b) & 3617 (HUD / DOJ)
legal_framework.applicability_94122: Anti-Discrimination & Subsidy Constraints (No General Federal % Cap Identified)
legal_framework.rule_summary: No general federal rent-increase percentage cap was identified in reviewed federal sources for unsubsidized private rentals; however, federal law strictly bars discriminatory rental terms/increases (§ 3604(b)) and coercion/retaliation (§ 3617) across protected classes, and program rules govern federal voucher/subsidized tenancies.

landlord_practices.dimension: Statutory Entity Exemptions (AB 1482 Single-Family / Condo Rule)
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: Under Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12(d)(5), REITs (IRC § 856), corporations, and LLCs with at least one corporate member are statutorily disqualified from the AB 1482 single-family/condo rent-cap exemption; public residential REITs report California local and state rent caps as binding regulatory limits in SEC Form 10-K filings.
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: Natural-person (or wholly individual-member LLC) owners can qualify for AB 1482's single-family/condo exemption ONLY on separately alienable single-family/condo units with mandatory written tenant notice—whereas covered pre-6/14/1979 multi-unit SF rentals remain subject to SF's 1.6% cap regardless of whether the owner is a corporation or an individual.

landlord_practices.dimension: SF Housing Inventory Reporting & Rent Increase License Portal Workflow
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: Properties with 10+ units were subject to mandatory SF Housing Inventory reporting first (operative July 1, 2022); the SF Rent Board provides a Bulk Excel Upload portal workflow specifically for portfolios reporting 5+ units.
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: Buildings with 1–9 units and condos phased in on March 1, 2023; the SF Rent Board instructs owners reporting fewer than 5 units NOT to use bulk upload templates and instead submit via the 'Individual Unit' portal workflow by March 1 annually.

landlord_practices.dimension: Algorithmic Revenue-Management Software & Antitrust / Local Prohibitions
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: U.S. DOJ and California AG antitrust complaints (Aug. 2024) document multi-state corporate landlord use of algorithmic pricing software (e.g., RealPage YieldStar/AIRM). In San Francisco, SF Admin. Code § 37.10C prohibits ANY landlord from using algorithmic devices analyzing non-public competitor data to set rents or occupancy.
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: Both corporate and individual SF landlords are subject to § 37.10C ($1,000/unit/month civil penalty + attorney's fees, with tenant-organization lawsuit standing effective Oct. 6, 2025) and must compute covered rent increases strictly from published SF Rent Board CPI schedules.

landlord_practices.dimension: Citywide Above-Cap Petition Filings (FY 2024–2025 Empirical Totals)
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: SF Rent Board FY 2024–2025 statistics show multi-unit concentration in formal passthrough filings: 209 Capital Improvement petitions covered 1,261 units (6.03 units/petition) and 42 Utility Passthrough Worksheets covered 849 units (20.21 units/filing), though the Rent Board report does not break filings out by corporate vs. individual entity type.
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: Citywide, Operating & Maintenance petitions totaled only 8 filings covering 32 units in FY 2024–2025; entity-level filing shares between corporate and individual SF owners are not published in official Rent Board tables.
landlord_practices.verified_metric: 209 CI petitions (1,261 units); 42 Utility worksheets (849 units)

landlord_practices.dimension: Official Counseling & Trade Association Access Listed by SF Rent Board
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: Large portfolios retain private compliance counsel and property-management compliance systems; SF Rent Board Form 590 also lists professional associations (San Francisco Apartment Association, California Apartment Association).
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: SF Rent Board Form 590 lists Small Property Owners of San Francisco Institute (SPOSFI), SF Apartment Association, Bar Association of SF Lawyer Referral Service, and the Rent Board's neutral counselor line (415-252-4600).
landlord_practices.verified_metric: SF Rent Board Form 590 Referral Listing

landlord_practices.dimension: Representative SF Renewal Frequency, Banking Rates & Notice-Error Rates by Owner Type
landlord_practices.corporate_reits: No official government survey or SF Rent Board statistical table publishes representative percentages comparing how often SF corporate vs. individual landlords take annual CPI increases, bank skipped years, or commit notice defects.
landlord_practices.individual_owners_sf: Left blank rather than generalized from anecdotes: while Topic 503 explains how skipped increases bank, official agencies do not publish comparative behavioral frequencies between individual and corporate SF landlords.

notice_protocol.step: Step 1 · Verify Parcel Coverage, Active Lease Terms & Retaliation Constraints
notice_protocol.requirement: Verify parcel/unit Rent Ordinance coverage, inspect the physical lease (no unilateral increase during an active fixed-term lease unless expressly permitted per Civ. Code § 827(a)), and confirm zero recent tenantability complaints/citations within 180 days (Civ. Code § 1942.5(a)) or retaliatory motive (§ 1942.5(d)).
notice_protocol.reasonable_reason_guidance: Documenting objective contract and habitability verification prior to notice creation reduces avoidable procedural defects.

notice_protocol.step: Step 2 · Confirm Active SF Rent Increase License Before Service & Effective Date
notice_protocol.requirement: Log into https://portal.sfrb.org, complete the current cycle's Housing Inventory filing for each unit, and retain timestamped confirmation of the active Rent Increase License BEFORE serving notice and BEFORE the effective date (also verify $59.00/unit Rent Board Fee payment).
notice_protocol.reasonable_reason_guidance: Without an active Rent Increase License on the effective date, an annual or banked increase on a covered SF unit cannot lawfully take effect.

notice_protocol.step: Step 3 · Verify Lawful Base Rent & Exact 12-Month Anniversary
notice_protocol.requirement: Verify current lawful base rent from the full payment/notice ledger and confirm ≥12 full months elapsed since tenancy start or last increase. Multiply ONLY base rent (excluding passthroughs or Rent Board fee) by the rate in effect on the EFFECTIVE date (1.6% through Feb. 28, 2027), with zero upward rounding.
notice_protocol.reasonable_reason_guidance: Under SF Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1), no cost-increase excuse is required for the published annual CPI adjustment. Never assert unpetitioned repair/tax costs to exceed 1.6%.

notice_protocol.step: Step 4 · Draft Written Notice With Neutral Statutory Citation & Itemization
notice_protocol.requirement: State in writing: (1) tenant names on lease & unit address, (2) verified current base rent, (3) exact dollar increase, (4) exact percentage, (5) new base rent, (6) effective date, and (7) separate itemization if any verified banked portion or separate $29.50 Rent Board Fee invoice is included.
notice_protocol.reasonable_reason_guidance: Neutral wording example: 'Annual allowable rent adjustment of 1.6% pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code § 37.3(a)(1) and the SF Rent Board published rate for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027.'

notice_protocol.step: Step 5 · Serve via Statutory Delivery Method & Retain Proof of Service
notice_protocol.requirement: Serve personally (Civ. Code § 827(b)(1)(A)) OR by first-class U.S. mail within California adding +5 calendar days (CCP § 1013(a)): minimum 30 days personal / 35 days CA mail if ≤10%; 90 days personal / 95 days CA mail if >10%. Email/text alone is invalid.
notice_protocol.reasonable_reason_guidance: Archive a signed Proof of Service, USPS certificate of mailing, and exact copy of the served notice in the unit record.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Active Rent Increase License on Effective Date
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Checks SF Rent Board Portal (portal.sfrb.org) to verify whether Housing Inventory reporting was completed and an active Rent Increase License existed on the effective date.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Notice is unenforceable; tenant may file a Tenant Summary Petition / Unlawful Rent Increase Petition at the Rent Board for restitution.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Fixed-Term Lease Contract Bar (Critical for Unit 1)
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Inspects the April 1, 2026 Unit 1 agreement to see if it created a fixed-term lease (e.g., 12 months through 3/31/2027) lacking a rent-increase clause.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Under Cal. Civ. Code § 827(a), a unilateral increase taking effect during an active fixed-term lease is invalid.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Confirms original occupant Tenant A1 still resides in Unit 1 and checks that zero extra fee/reset was imposed for replacement co-occupant Tenant A4.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Any vacancy reset or roommate surcharge violates Civ. Code § 1954.53(d)(2)–(3) and Rent Board Rules §§ 6.13–6.14.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Verifies at least 12 full calendar months elapsed since tenancy start and since the effective date of the prior lawful rent increase.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Premature effective date invalidates the rent increase notice.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Rate Window Matching Effective Date (Not Service Date)
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Checks whether the effective date falls inside March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (1.6%). Notices taking effect on/after March 1, 2027 are governed by the 2027–2028 rate.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Any excess above the rate governing the effective date is unlawful and refundable.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Base-Rent-Only Exact Penny Calculation (Zero Upward Rounding)
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Verifies exact base-rent multiplication ($3,995 × 0.016 = $63.92; $3,150 × 0.016 = $50.40 if $3,150 is current base rent) with zero upward rounding and zero passthroughs/fees in base rent.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Rounding up (even by cents) exceeds the allowable cap and subjects overcharges to Rent Board refund orders.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Demands full 2019–2026 ledger proof, checks the 24-full-month banking rule, checks for unlawful compounding or forfeited shifted-anniversary slices, and checks notice itemization.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Unproven, compounded, or unbanked percentages are disallowed in a Tenant Unlawful Rent Increase Petition.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Statutory Service Method & Day-Count (30/35 vs. 90/95 Calendar Days)
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Checks postmark date, CCP § 1013 +5-day CA mail extension, 90+5 day requirement if >10%, and confirms notice was NOT served solely by email/text.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Improper service or short lead time renders the notice defective under Civ. Code § 827.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Checks whether utility, water bond, GO bond, or repair charges were added without an approved Rent Board Petition or attached official Passthrough Worksheet.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Rent Board invalidation and full restitution of unauthorized charges.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Reviews repair complaints/citations within 180 days (Civ. Code § 1942.5(a)), protected tenant organizing/rights exercise (§ 1942.5(d)), and SF DBI Notices of Violation.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Statutory retaliation defense plus exposure to actual/punitive damages and statutory attorney's fees.

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.audit_point: Cross-Unit Fair Housing & Harassment Review (Unit 1 vs. Unit 2)
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Tests whether any disparity between Unit 1 and Unit 2 stems from objective contract/anniversary eligibility rather than protected traits or bad-faith coercion (FHA; FEHA; SF § 37.10B).
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: CRD/HUD administrative inquiry or civil action (with treble damages / $1,000 minimum and mandatory tenant attorney's fees under § 37.10B).

lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.what_tenant_lawyer_checks: Verifies rent was calculated from the public SF Rent Board CPI schedule rather than prohibited non-public competitor pricing software.
lawyer_scrutiny_checklist.defect_consequence: Civil action by tenant, City Attorney, or SF tenants' rights organization ($1,000/unit/month penalty + attorney's fees).

tenant_legal_directory.scope_of_service: Official SF.gov eviction resource: free legal help is provided by EDC for tenants who receive eviction court papers (unlawful detainer), rather than universal pre-notice review of routine rent increases.

one_vs_both_matrix.scenario: Scenario 1 — Unit 1's April 1, 2026 Agreement Is an Active 12-Month Fixed-Term Lease (through March 31, 2027), while Unit 2 Is Eligible Month-to-Month
one_vs_both_matrix.legal_permissibility: Permissible & Contractually Required to Defer Unit 1 Until Fixed Term Ends
one_vs_both_matrix.discrimination_analysis: Under Cal. Civ. Code § 827(a), Unit 1 cannot be unilaterally increased during an active fixed-term lease. Applying a neutral building-wide policy—adjusting each unit at its first lawful month-to-month contract/anniversary eligibility date using the published SF Rent Board rate—bases timing strictly on objective contract status rather than protected traits (though no policy guarantees zero inquiries without case-specific counsel review).

one_vs_both_matrix.scenario: Scenario 2 — Both Unit 1 and Unit 2 Are Independently Verified as Eligible Month-to-Month Tenancies
one_vs_both_matrix.legal_permissibility: Uniform Per-Unit Formula Application Is Permissible & Advisable for Consistency
one_vs_both_matrix.discrimination_analysis: Applying the same published 1.6% SF Rent Board formula to all eligible month-to-month units under a written, neutral schedule avoids unexplained cross-unit disparities under FHA (42 U.S.C. § 3604(b)), FEHA (Gov. Code § 12955), and SF § 37.10B, provided each unit independently clears lease, ledger, license, and § 1942.5 retaliation checks.

one_vs_both_matrix.scenario: Scenario 3 — Raising Only One Eligible Month-to-Month Unit While Skipping Another Similary Situated Eligible Unit Without Objective Criteria
one_vs_both_matrix.legal_permissibility: Not Automatically Unlawful, But Increases Selective-Treatment Questioning Risk
one_vs_both_matrix.discrimination_analysis: No statute mandates raising every unit simultaneously, so deferring one unit for a documented, non-protected reason is lawful; however, unexplained selective increases in a multi-unit property make it harder to rebut disparate-treatment or harassment allegations if households differ across FEHA's 19+ protected traits.

one_vs_both_matrix.scenario: Scenario 4 — Raising Both Units When One Unit Has an Active Fixed Lease, Unresolved Habitability Complaint, or Ledger Defect
one_vs_both_matrix.legal_permissibility: Impermissible — Uniformity Never Cures a Contract Breach or Retaliatory Notice
one_vs_both_matrix.discrimination_analysis: Raising a second unit provides zero defense if an increase violates a fixed-term lease (Civ. Code § 827(a)) or falls within Cal. Civ. Code § 1942.5(a)/(d) anti-retaliation prohibitions. Every unit must pass compliance verification independently.
